part.text:
Fixed. The issue was in `bitposCommand` (src/bitops.c:1787), which looked up the key before parsing the optional `start`/`end`/`BIT|BYTE` arguments — so `BITPOS missing-key <illegal args>` returned `0` instead of an error. I restructured it to validate all arguments first (mirroring the pattern already used by `bitcountCommand`), then look up the key:

- Parse `bit`, `start`, `end`, and the `BIT|BYTE` unit (with `ERR syntax error` for malformed syntax) before any key lookup
- Compute the default `end` (end of string) after the key lookup, when `end` isn't given
- Keep the missing-key semantics (`0` for bit=0, `-1` for bit=1) intact

Verification: `unit/bitops` now passes all tests (previously `BITPOS will illegal arguments` and `BITPOS against non-integer value` failed), and `unit/type/string`, `unit/other`, `unit/keyspace`, and `unit/protocol` also pass with no regressions.
